key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of unseen perovskite samples, enabling faster stability screening than conventional aging tests.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to reduce experimental turnaround in perovskite solar-cell development by predicting stability from early time-series measurements.
method: Collected 86k+ photoluminescence spectra from 167 perovskite samples under heat and light stress
Featurized spectra with a physics-informed model to preserve interpretable stability descriptors
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to forecast future PL intensity for unseen materials
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on a diverse dataset of 167 metal halide perovskites and reportedly generalized across material groups while outperforming baseline benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and coverage of the training dataset, so extrapolation to new chemistries, stress conditions, or measurement setups should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
